name: Swastika Castal Ltd
tagline: Vadodara nano-cap aluminium-casting maker (ROCE ~33%) that is one of a handful of approved Indian vendors for GIS substation enclosures up to 420 kV - a genuine grid-capex + import-substitution optionality, but just one year listed and Rs ~35 Cr of revenue
business_overview: Swastika Castal (incorporated 1996, Vadodara; BSE SME, listed 28 July 2025 at Rs 65) makes high-precision aluminium castings via sand, gravity die and centrifugal processes for electrical equipment, railways, diesel engines and general industrial use. The differentiated end-market is aluminium enclosures/castings for Gas-Insulated Switchgear (GIS) substations - the sealed aluminium 'plumbing' that houses SF6-insulated HV conductors. Per the ValuePickr thread, Swastika appears on Adani Energy Solutions' approved vendor list for GIS aluminium enclosures rated up to 420 kV, a segment still largely import-dependent (mostly Chinese suppliers). Recent client additions include Trench Electric (Siemens Energy group) and Kuvag.
fundamentals_table: ~Rs 97 Cr (Screener; ~Rs 67-97 Cr across sources, up ~47% in 1 year)
Rs 35.4 Cr revenue / Rs 3.28 Cr PAT
BSE SME, 28 Jul 2025 @ Rs 65; CMP ~Rs 91 at thread date
fundamentals_narrative: Returns profile is strong on paper - ROE ~28%, ROCE ~33% at the July-2025 IPO - but the absolute base is tiny (Rs 35 Cr revenue, Rs 3.3 Cr PAT) and the track record as a listed company is barely one year. D/E ~0.85 is high for a business this small. Fresh screener data was thin this pass; the investable question is whether GIS-enclosure and export/import-substitution orders can scale revenue several-fold while holding the current return ratios. No recent-quarter numbers were available to confirm an inflection - the thesis rests on the approved-vendor status and stated demand signals, not yet on delivered growth.
technical_read: Not pulled (nano-cap SME, illiquid; not a Tier-A-confirmation candidate this pass). Up ~47% over the trailing year per Screener; listed at Rs 65, traded ~Rs 91 at the time of the latest thread post.

value_chain.theme: Grid / transmission equipment (transformers, HV switchgear, HVDC, CRGO, insulators)
value_chain.position: Tier-2 component supplier - aluminium castings / enclosures feeding GIS switchgear and HV power-equipment OEMs (Adani Energy Solutions approved vendor; Trench Electric, Kuvag, Quality Power ecosystem)
value_chain.bottleneck_node: Precision aluminium castings for HV GIS enclosures (up to 420 kV) - currently import-dependent, mostly from China; qualified Indian capacity is scarce, which is the pricing-power point
adjacent_peers: MM Forgings / other aluminium & ferrous foundries
value_chain.note: The value-chain edge is qualification, not scale: being an approved 420 kV GIS-enclosure vendor is a multi-year barrier, and India's grid/substation capex plus a push to localise Chinese-sourced castings is a real demand tailwind. Risk: SF6 phase-out could reshape GIS design over the long run (though replacement-gas GIS still uses aluminium enclosures), and supply-side capacity is being added by multiple small foundries.
